summary: A local context-compression layer that sits between a coding agent and the model, shrinking what the agent sends (tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks) and trimming what the model writes back -- without deleting anything. summary: A tool that learns a website's internal network requests and re-exposes them as operations an agent calls over HTTP, skipping browser automation entirely. Calls then run in tiers, starting with a direct Node fetch (no browser). Learned operations go into a shared catalog (a Cloudflare Worker stores specs and success/fail votes -- it never proxies traffic; calls leave from your machine, logins stay local). Ships ~30 read operations across 14 sites (Goodreads, Google Flights, Hacker News, LinkedIn, X, Instagram, others). The poster is the project's author (Charles Zheng), demonstrating his own tool -- provenance is …

author: @reporadarai
title_or_hook: Edge0: SSD-streamed MoE inference, 35B in 2.9 GB
summary: An open-source inference framework that runs a 35B-parameter MoE model with ~2.9 GiB peak active memory by memory-mapping expert weights from SSD and streaming only the experts a token needs. Three mechanisms per its docs: SSD expert offload (SafetensorsMmap + a cross-layer LRU SharedExpertCache), a trained per-layer prerouter that predicts the next token's experts one step ahead (the source of the claimed up-to-59% decode boost), and an unmerged LoRA that recovers most int4 quantization loss. Ships two checkpoints: Edge0-35B-A3B-preview (from Qwen3.5-MoE) and Edge0-8B-A1B-preview (from Ling-3.0-tiny). Measured in project material: 2.9 GiB / 20.4 tok/s for 35B vs 18.2 GiB for a fully resident int4 engine.
engine_training_value: Direct: the prerouter is trained on labeled expert-activation sequences -- (context → next-token expert set) pairs. That dataset shape, and the hit-rate/throughput labels Edge0 publishes per benchmark (HumanEval, MMLU-Pro in its tables), are a template for training GSE's own "which features will matter next" routing layer. Data lives in the repo + paper; labels exist (activation traces are self-labeling).

summary: An open-source serving engine that runs frontier-scale Mixture-of-Experts models on a personal machine by treating GPU + CPU + system RAM + interconnect as one elastic inference platform: bandwidth-adaptive CPU-GPU co-execution, a global LRU expert cache, streamed prefill, and a fast weight format. author: @githubsignals
title_or_hook: gpu-unlock: Linux kernel module that removes GeForce tensor-core half-rate cap
summary: A Linux kernel module by Zagitta that runs from the initramfs before the stock NVIDIA driver binds the card, writes two internal speed selectors (SS0 0x88888888, SS1 0x8), performs a function-level reset, and lets the unmodified driver load -- removing NVIDIA's product-segmentation cap that runs GeForce tensor cores at half rate for FP16/BF16/TF32 math with FP32 accumulation (the same silicon in RTX A-series pro cards runs full rate). Not a patched driver, not a VBIOS flash, so driver updates do not undo it. It does nothing unless gpu_unlock.targets= is on the kernel command line.
engine_training_value: Indirect but real: prefill throughput is the cost driver for running the reasoning engine's L1-L5 traces locally; a verified 25-55% prefill gain changes which local models are viable as trace generators/judges. No dataset or labels ship with the tool itself.

Modern versions add AI assistance: SAM/EfficientSAM point-to-polygon, and text-to-annotation via YOLO-World and SAM3. Any GSE computer-vision feature (formation recognition, player tracking ground truth, telestration targets) needs exactly what Labelme produces -- polygon/mask labels in COCO/VOC JSON, from GSE's own frames. Labels are created by the user; the tool's job is making them cheap.

author: @simplifyinai
title_or_hook: PageIndex: vectorless, reasoning-based RAG over a document tree
summary: An open-source RAG framework that deletes the vector stack: no embeddings, no chunking, no vector DB. For each long document (PDF/Markdown) an LLM builds a hierarchical tree index -- a smart table of contents where each node carries a title, a summary, and a pointer to the raw text -- and at query time an LLM reasons its way down the tree to the relevant sections, then answers with page-level citations and an explicit retrieval trace. The headline number: 98.7% on FinanceBench -- with the correction every secondary source repeats: that score belongs to Mafin 2.5, VectifyAI's finance system built on PageIndex, on a benchmark of structured SEC filings, run by the team itself, with no independent replication and no …
engine_training_value: Direct for the reasoning layer: (question → tree path taken → section → answer) traces are labeled retrieval data -- they teach where in a document an answer lives, which is trainable supervision for GSE's own document reasoning. The FinanceBench result is itself a labeled benchmark row (system × benchmark × score) for the fleet's model/tool routing records.

title_or_hook: The agent writes the scene as code, renders it, and revises it -- @gittrend.io (recreator; origin: Voyager) -- resolved: vork
summary: The caption describes, almost word for word, vork: a headless 3D and VFX engine built for agents instead of humans. There is no editor, no timeline, no window. An agent writes a scene as a JSON document / code (meshes, lights, cameras, materials, animation), runs a render command, looks at the resulting image, and revises the code until the frame is right. The kernel deliberately holds only what an agent cannot write on the fly -- geometry, ray queries, GPU execution -- while materials, cameras, light propagation, simulation, and compositing are small programs the agent writes per shot (its showcase example bends light around a black hole inside the scene program, not the engine). Written in Rust and Slang; renders …

For the sports prediction engine: the §5(c) simulation-visualization path would turn existing labeled simulation outputs into reviewable film, which improves human and agent grading of those outputs; it creates no new sports labels itself. Filed honestly at that strength. ---

author: @asharasjad
title_or_hook: ARLoop: fully-open looped transformers that reuse their own layers, with the training recipe published
summary: ARLoop is a looped transformer architecture: instead of stacking distinct layers, it repeatedly applies one shared set of layers (recurrence), and at each pass the input to a layer is built by attention over depth -- the layer selectively pulls from earlier passes' intermediate representations (attention residuals) rather than receiving one merged residual stream. The paper's key finding is that a sliding window over recent depth matches or beats attending to the full history at larger recurrence depths, which caps the cost of the mechanism. The release is genuinely fully-open in the sense the post claims: training code, data-processing code, intermediate checkpoints, and final models are all published, which is exactly the part most looped-LLM releases withhold. Verified figures from …
engine_training_value: Real, two kinds. (i) The published training trajectory (checkpoints × benchmarks) is labeled data about how recurrent depth converts to task gains -- usable as prior evidence when the engine weighs iterative-refinement designs. (ii) If the §7 test proceeds, its 50-item scored set becomes a labeled (small-open-model, task, correct/incorrect) row set for the routing dataset. For the sports prediction model itself: no sports labels; the value is architectural and routing-level, filed at that strength.

summary: OpenBot is a self-hosted template (its README's own word: "a template, not a product") for running AI coworkers inside your own infrastructure. It ships 13 example coworkers as configuration.

author: @githubsignals
title_or_hook: BitDecoding FP4: native FP4 KV-cache decoding, ~2.4-3.0× serving throughput (VERIFIED, hardware-gated)
summary: An algorithm-system co-design for running an LLM's KV cache in native 4-bit floating point (NVFP4 / MXFP4) on FP4 Tensor Cores without the usual accuracy collapse. Three named mechanisms from the paper abstract: (a) Dual-Residual Query Quantization -- splits the query into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; (b) Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling -- prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; (c) Outlier-Aware Key Quantization -- static smoothing + Hadamard rotation + scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. The poster (@githubsignals) is a repo-drop aggregator/recreator; the origin is the paper + repo below.
engine_training_value: Indirect but real: cheaper long-context inference lowers the cost of generating training/rollout data and of running long-context reasoning over game corpora. The technique itself teaches no metric or label -- the value is inference economics for the training loop, not a dataset.

author: @simplifyinai
title_or_hook: Graphify + Obsidian + Claude Code: docs → knowledge graph → vault
summary: Graphify is an open-source CLI + AI-assistant skill that turns a folder of code, docs, papers, and media into a queryable knowledge graph instead of leaving an agent to grep raw files. Three passes: (a) a deterministic tree-sitter AST pass over code (36 languages; classes, functions, imports, call graphs; no LLM, no API key); (b) local faster-whisper transcription of audio/video; (c) Claude subagents extracting concepts, relationships, and rationale from docs/papers/images/transcripts. The merged NetworkX graph is clustered with Leiden community detection (no embeddings/vector DB), and every edge carries a provenance label: EXTRACTED (from the AST), INFERRED (model-generated), or AMBIGUOUS. Outputs: graph.html, graph.json (persistent), GRAPH_REPORT.md (god nodes, surprising connections, suggested questions), and exports to Obsidian vault, Neo4j, FalkorDB, GraphML, SVG, and a markdown wiki. Installs as a skill in 17+ harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Antigravity, Hermes, others) and exposes an MCP endpoint. The post's workflow maps 145 pages of Claude Code docs, exports the map as an Obsidian vault (graphify --obsidian), and has Claude pull source text back into each note. Free and open source; license conflict in secondary sources (Apache 2.0 vs MIT) -- verify the repo LICENSE before integration. The poster's $10K/mo claim is UNVERIFIED.
engine_training_value: Indirect: a provenance-labelled graph over the research corpus is retrieval infrastructure for the reasoning layer, not training data. The graph's own edge labels (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS with sources) are a labelled dataset shape -- claim-provenance triples the fleet could learn verification behaviour from. No metric or label for the prediction engine itself.
